extracted.intended_audience: NPR editorial staff, reporters, editors, producers, hosts, freelancers and other contributors who shape journalistic content
extracted.subtask_description: Organization-specific ethics and editorial standards for producing trustworthy journalism at NPR, covering principles (accuracy, fairness, independence, etc.), procedural scope, and topical guidance (anonymous sources, AI, social media). Intended to guide editorial judgment across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Our Mission
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of NPR, in partnership with its member stations, is to create a more informed public by reporting, producing, acquiring and distributing news, information and other content that meet the highest standards of public service in journalism and cultural expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the purpose against which editorial decisions should be measured: public service, deeper understanding and appreciation of events, ideas and culture domestically and globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: NPR aspires to the heights of public service and holds itself to core principles of honesty, integrity, independence, accuracy, contextual truth, transparency, respect and fairness. Diversity of voices is essential to truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The handbook is a foundation for staff to consider often-competing principles and exercise judgment, not a prescriptive list of do's and don'ts.

rubrics_metrics.name: About the handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the handbook's intent as guidance for editorial staff and how it will be used and evolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the handbook is a living document; staff should consult it and seek advice when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking advice and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial staff should seek advice and approval when confronting ethical or procedural questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the handbook as a baseline and consult Standards & Practices or supervisors for difficult decisions (implied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is covered
rubrics_metrics.description: All editorial staff are bound by this guidance — defined as those who shape journalistic or creative direction, including leadership, managers, reporters, editors, newscasters, producers, visual and data journalists, hosts, interns, freelancers and NPR events/promotions staff who shape editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-editorial newsroom staff follow the NPR Code of Conduct; contributors should adhere depending on the content they create.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our purpose is to pursue the truth. Diligent verification is critical. We take great care to ensure that statements of fact are both correct and in context, rigorously challenge claims we encounter and assumptions we bring, and present the fullest version of the truth we can deliver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Devote resources and skills to information gathered and verified ourselves; avoid errors of fact and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in our reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply rigorous verification practices in reporting to ensure factual correctness and contextual truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize first-hand reporting and careful challenge of claims and assumptions (page lists this as a subtopic under Accuracy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Using information from non-NPR sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to handle, attribute and verify material that originates outside NPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure external information is checked and clearly attributed; be cautious about relying on unverified third-party materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy online
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply accuracy standards to digital content, recognizing different formats and speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain verification and context online despite immediacy and platform constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in visual journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual elements must be accurate and presented in context; visuals should not mislead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat images, video and graphics with the same verification and contextual standards as text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: To tell the truest story possible, treat those interviewed and reported on with scrupulous fairness; gather responses from subjects of criticism or negative assertions, and be faithful to people’s meaning when quoting or editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek strongest arguments on all sides in matters of controversy; aim for truth rather than appearance of balance or pleasing subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in presenting the news
rubrics_metrics.description: Present news in ways that consider nuance and clarity and do not distort meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit for time and clarity while remaining faithful to interviewees' meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in reporting and interviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Make every effort to gather responses from those who are subjects of criticism and to represent their views accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid misrepresentation through selective quoting; pursue comprehensive sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness to colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat colleagues with professionalism and fairness in the workplace and editorial processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fosters an internal culture that supports fair coverage and collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair use
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect legal and ethical boundaries around use of copyrighted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply fair use considerations when incorporating third-party content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Do our best to report thoroughly and tell stories comprehensively; explain what we don't yet know and work to fill gaps in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid errors of omission and partial truths; include diverse voices and divergent views that contribute to informed debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telling the full story
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, deliver the context and breadth needed to understand a story fully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to provide all answers, be transparent about gaps and seek to address them in future reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific reporting practices to avoid incomplete narratives and to include necessary context and voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize comprehensive sourcing and context; recognize constraints of time/space and compensate through transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must be genuine and candid, attribute information clearly, avoid hyperbole and sensational conjecture, and not mix fiction with news reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed hypotheticals must be revealed; deception (e.g., disguising identity) is allowed only in rare public-safety cases after rigorous deliberation and must be fully disclosed when the story is told.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty in reporting and interviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Be candid and straightforward in interactions with sources and in reporting facts derived from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute information to its sources and avoid misleading editing or representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty in presenting information
rubrics_metrics.description: Present facts without deception and make clear what is known, what is inferred, and what is opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensationalism and clearly label analysis versus reported fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty in visual journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Images and visual storytelling must not deceive and should be honestly presented and attributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not manipulate visuals in ways that mislead the audience; disclose staging or reenactment when used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty online
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain candid attribution and avoid deceptive online practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same honesty standards to web and social formats as to broadcast and print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary allegiance is to the public; any personal or professional interests that conflict with that allegiance risk compromising credibility. Disclose conflicts and, when necessary, recuse from coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not skew reports for personal gain, NPR’s bottom line, or to please funders; editorial decisions are made by journalists, not funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant in disclosing circumstances where loyalties may be divided (including family members' interests) and recuse when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose to supervisors and the public as needed; avoid coverage that could be perceived as conflicted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interacting with funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a firewall between editorial decisions and those who provide financial support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow funders to influence coverage; disclose relevant relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owning our news agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists decide what to cover and how; editorial control should remain independent of funders or commercial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act to protect editorial autonomy in story selection and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside work
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on outside employment and activities that might conflict with journalistic duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose and manage outside work to prevent conflicts with public-first allegiance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paying our own way
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards about accepting travel, gifts or sponsored opportunities that might compromise independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer paying own way or disclosing and managing exceptions to avoid perceived influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working for NPR while keeping the public first
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must prioritize the public interest over organizational or personal interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All decisions should be guided by duty to the public and transparency about potential competing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff may have personal opinions but must comport themselves to honor professional impartiality so that reporting and analysis are not unduly influenced by personal views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggressively challenge personal perspectives and pursue diverse viewpoints to present truth as completely as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality in our personal lives
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that personal actions and statements can affect public perception of NPR; comport oneself accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept some professional limitations in personal life to preserve public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality in our journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce reporting and analysis that transcend individual biases and treat all views fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to present balanced, evidence-based reporting rather than mere appearance of balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal as much as practicable about how NPR discovers and verifies facts; make decision-making clear to the public, especially in tough choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose relationships that might influence coverage and explain reporting processes to help the public evaluate work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revealing our process
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the newsroom’s methods visible when possible so audiences can assess reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain sourcing, verification steps, and editorial reasoning in stories or accompanying material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Special guidance on use of anonymous sources under transparency and verification expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit use of anonymity, verify information independently, and explain rationale to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Take full responsibility for work, welcome questions and criticism from the public, respond when possible, and correct mistakes forthrightly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use feedback to learn; be ready to answer for reporting choices and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: When mistakes occur, correct them openly and reflect on causes to avoid repetition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt, visible corrections strengthen credibility; document and learn from errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interacting with the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to stakeholders and engage constructively with questions and criticisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public engagement is part of accountability and can improve journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability online
rubrics_metrics.description: Be responsive and responsible in digital interactions and correction practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply accountability standards to social media, web comments and other online venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize legal responsibilities and liabilities as part of taking responsibility for work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult legal counsel when necessary and correct or clarify items that raise legal concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat everyone affected by journalism with decency and compassion; be civil, avoid arrogance, listen, and minimize undue harm — especially to vulnerable people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sensitive to cultural differences and privacy; ask tough questions to seek answers, not to confront.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for sources and subjects of coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect privacy and dignity of sources and subjects while fulfilling journalistic obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take special care with those who are vulnerable or suffering; minimize harm where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect in sensitive circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra care and sensitivity in reporting on trauma, victims, or culturally fraught topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance public interest with compassion and privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for our audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat audience members with decency and consideration in tone, content and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid condescension and respect audience diversity and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Marry important truths with engaging narrative; take pride in craftsmanship of storytelling and quality of words, sounds and images to illuminate the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit for impact and clarity, not to slant or distort; avoid sensationalism and shallow sentimentality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive for compelling narrative that conveys truth faithfully and powerfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use storytelling craft to illuminate significance without compromising accuracy or fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in news judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply strong editorial judgment to select and shape stories of significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize coverage that serves the public and avoids sensational distractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Putting Principles Into Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles often reinforce and sometimes conflict; staff should balance them against one another and use judgment to honor NPR’s mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace complexity, provoke discussion and deliberation, and foster a culture that empowers staff to apply conscience to daily decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: How the handbook applies to you
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical note that staff should consider how the handbook's principles govern their specific roles and decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages personal application and reflection on ethical responsibilities in one’s work.

rubrics_metrics.name: How the handbook will evolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that standards and guidance will change and the handbook will be updated accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect revisions and ongoing discussion to address new challenges and technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Guidance (Standards & Practices Outbox)
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasional notes from the Standards & Practices editor expanding on handbook topics and explaining how NPR handles issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these editorials for concrete examples and deeper explanation of how principles are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Sections / topical guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Dedicated topical guidance on practical issues such as Anonymous sourcing, Attribution, Diversity, Generative artificial intelligence, Social Media, Speaking Appearances, Visual journalism, and platform-specific considerations (Facebook, Flipboard, Email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to these special sections for detailed rules and examples on handling specific recurring ethical and technical issues.
